description: Frank Russo submits a formal application for the $2,500 small business stabilization grant offered to auto-sector businesses with documented revenue decline. Documentation submitted: prior year revenue records showing total loss of student enrollment, valid business license, one-page business description noting both the impact of the AV transition and his active pivot toward AV literacy instruction through the district adult ed program. Frank's application explicitly notes that he is using the stabilization funds to support a rebuild, not a delay — he references the curriculum he has developed and the pending meeting with the adult ed intake coordinator. He qualifies on all stated criteria: auto-sector adjacent business, licensed operation, revenue decline well above the 10% threshold.
notes: Frank has all documentation assembled from research conducted in tick 7. The application is complete and submitted this tick. If approved, $2,500 extends his runway by approximately 0.8 months — meaningful at his current 4.2-month runway. Frank's inclusion of the AV literacy pivot in the application is both honest and strategically sound: it demonstrates that the grant would support productive economic reintegration, not mere delay. The RoboRide price drop to $0.12/mile announced this tick strengthens the case for his pivot — the AV transition is accelerating and documented in real-time.
